questions.question: Q1. What does the thrust-to-weight ratio (TWR) of a multirotor tell you?

answers.b: How many times its own weight the craft can push in thrust

explanations.a: Incorrect — endurance depends on efficiency and battery capacity, not TWR directly.
explanations.b: Correct — TWR = total thrust / weight; it is the dimensionless measure of how much lifting/accelerating authority the craft has.
explanations.c: Incorrect — top speed depends on aerodynamics and tilt, not the static TWR.
explanations.d: Incorrect — range is a radio property, unrelated to TWR.

questions.question: Q2. What is the minimum thrust-to-weight ratio needed for a drone to leave the ground?

answers.b: Exactly 1.0 is plenty for good control

explanations.a: Incorrect — below 1.0 the thrust cannot even equal the weight.
explanations.b: Incorrect — at exactly 1.0 the craft hovers only at full throttle with zero margin; it cannot manoeuvre.
explanations.c: Correct — TWR must exceed 1 to lift off, and around 2 or more is needed for controllable flight with manoeuvre headroom.
explanations.d: Incorrect — TWR > 10 is extreme racing territory, far beyond the minimum.

questions.question: Q3. Why is hovering at roughly 50% throttle considered ideal?

answers.b: It leaves symmetric authority to climb and to descend
answers.c: It is the only throttle the motors can sustain

explanations.a: Incorrect — minimum power draw is not at 50% throttle.
explanations.b: Correct — a mid-range hover keeps roughly equal thrust reserve above (to climb / correct) and below (to descend), giving balanced control authority.
explanations.c: Incorrect — motors run across the whole range.
explanations.d: Incorrect — throttle does not set the radio link.

questions.question: Q4. What is the 'control margin' of a hovering multirotor?

answers.a: The throttle reserve available above the hover point for manoeuvres
answers.b: The distance to the nearest obstacle
answers.c: The gap between motor and ESC ratings
answers.d: The tolerance on the propeller diameter

explanations.a: Correct — control margin is the unused throttle above hover, the thrust reserve the stabilisation loop and pilot draw on to climb and reject disturbances.
explanations.b: Incorrect — that is a navigation clearance, not control margin.
explanations.c: Incorrect — that is a component-rating headroom.
explanations.d: Incorrect — that is a manufacturing tolerance.

questions.question: Q5. How does a propeller's thrust vary with its rotational speed (RPM)?

answers.c: Thrust is proportional to RPM squared
answers.d: Thrust is proportional to the square root of RPM

explanations.a: Incorrect — faster props clearly make more thrust.
explanations.b: Incorrect — the relationship is steeper than linear.
explanations.c: Correct — propeller thrust scales with the square of RPM (T proportional to RPM^2), which is why the thrust-vs-throttle curve is quadratic.
explanations.d: Incorrect — it grows faster than linearly, not slower.

questions.question: Q6. What happens to the thrust-to-weight ratio as you add payload to a drone?

answers.b: It falls, because total weight increases while max thrust is fixed

explanations.a: Incorrect — adding weight cannot increase TWR.
explanations.b: Correct — TWR = thrust / weight; payload raises the weight while the motors' maximum thrust is unchanged, so TWR drops.
explanations.d: Incorrect — it decreases toward 1, not infinity.

questions.question: Q7. In rotor theory, what does the 'figure of merit' (FoM) represent?

answers.a: The ratio of ideal hover power to the actual power a real rotor needs
answers.b: The maximum RPM of the motor

explanations.a: Correct — FoM (typically ~0.7) measures how close a real rotor comes to the ideal momentum-theory hover power; real losses make it less than 1.
explanations.b: Incorrect — that is an RPM limit.
explanations.c: Incorrect — blade count is a geometry choice.
explanations.d: Incorrect — that is a battery C-rating.

questions.question: Q8. For a fixed weight, how does a larger propeller disk area affect hover efficiency?

answers.b: It makes hovering more efficient (more lift per watt)
answers.c: It has no effect on efficiency
answers.d: It only matters at full throttle

explanations.a: Incorrect — small disks must accelerate air harder, wasting power.
explanations.b: Correct — a larger disk moves more air at a lower velocity for the same thrust, so the induced hover power drops and efficiency (g/W) rises.
explanations.c: Incorrect — disk area is central to induced power.
explanations.d: Incorrect — the benefit is strongest at hover.

questions.question: Q9. In momentum theory, how does the ideal hover power scale with thrust?

answers.a: Linearly with thrust (P proportional to T)
answers.b: With thrust to the 1.5 power (P proportional to T^1.5)
answers.c: With the square of thrust (P proportional to T^2)

explanations.a: Incorrect — power rises faster than linearly with thrust.
explanations.b: Correct — momentum theory gives P = T^1.5 / sqrt(2 rho A), so power grows with thrust to the three-halves power; doubling weight more than doubles hover power.
explanations.d: Incorrect — heavier craft clearly need more power.

questions.question: Q10. Hover efficiency is commonly expressed in which units?

explanations.a: Incorrect — that is the inverse; lower is not better in an intuitive sense.
explanations.b: Correct — efficiency is the lift produced per unit of electrical power, grams per watt; higher means longer endurance.
explanations.d: Incorrect — that is a conductance-like ratio, unrelated to lift efficiency.
